intro.title: Legacy code & rewrites
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a decision-making framework to evaluate whether a piece of legacy software should be refactored or completely rewritten. You will learn the core concepts of technical debt, risk assessment, and cost-benefit analysis as they apply to legacy systems. The main constructs involved are decision matrices and weighted scoring models, which help structure your evaluation. This beginner-friendly lesson will guide you through creating a clear, logical process to make informed engineering leadership choices about legacy code.
intro.usecase: Legacy code and rewrites are critical considerations when maintaining enterprise software systems like banking platforms, e-commerce backends, or healthcare record systems. Developers encounter this when modernizing outdated user interfaces—such as replacing a legacy dashboard with a React-based version while preserving existing business logic. Practical scenarios include incrementally refactoring a monolithic order processing system into microservices, or updating a legacy form validation library without breaking existing customer workflows. These decisions directly impact system stability, team velocity, and business continuity during technical transitions.
